findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed no signed employee health reporting agreement present in the facility. The manager of the facility was not present during the inspection, and staff were not knowledgeable of the location of required paperwork. Ensure there is a CFPM present at all times that can direct that can direct inspectors to required documentation. Inspectors provided a blank copy of the employee health reporting agreement to make copies and have all staff members sign employee health reporting agreements. A follow up will be conducted on October 1, 2026 to ensure these forms are signed and available for view.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment:
1st Repeat Violation

Inspectors observed no Certified Food Protection Manager present during the inspection. Ensure that there is at least one CFPM present during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a staff member handle the cash register with gloved hands and switch to new gloves without handwashing. Failure to wash between tasks occurred multiple times throughout the inspection. Education was conducted regarding proper hand washing practices. Ensure staff are removing gloves to handle electronic devices (cash register) or money, and washing hands thoroughly before donning new gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the active sanitizer bucket to measure 50ppm with a test strip. A staff member was informed and the bucket was replaced. Ensure the bucket is monitored frequently with a test strip and replaced often, as the chemical in the bucket will evaporate over time. The new bucket measured 200ppm quaternary ammonia with a test strip.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed black biological growth and rust present on the interior baffles of the ice machine. A staff member was informed and stated that the manager is responsible for cleaning the machine. The machine was last cleaned on 8/3/2026. Ensure this ice machine is cleaned and sanitized as frequently as necessary to prevent an accumulation of soil. A follow-up will be conducted on September 21, 2026 to ensure the interior of the machine is clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed rodent droppings in the cabinet below the soda machine in the self-service area of the facility. This cabinet also contained a glue trap which was observed free of pests. There were no sign of rodents in any other areas of the facility. A follow-up will be conducted on September 21, 2026 to ensure the droppings have been removed. Inspectors recommend adding dates of placement to the glue traps for monitoring purposes.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed two boxes of soda syrup in the back storage area to be stored directly on the ground. All food items must be stored at least 6” off the ground to prevent contamination or pest encroachment. Ensure these boxes are properly stored prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed white biological growth on the wire shelving in the walk-in cooler. Staff were informed that the shelves must remain clean to sight and touch at all times. Ensure these shelves are deep cleaned and sanitized prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed a staff member to have no food handler certification available. The staff member claimed he has worked here for “a few months.” Food handler certification is required within 30 days of hire. Ensure all staff are properly certified prior to the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There wasn’t a Certified Food Protection Manager present during the inspection. Ensure that there is at least one CFPM present during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Several TCS foods stored in the prep cooler next to the drive thru window lacked proper date marking. These items include but aren't limited to sauces, sliced cheeses, and deli meats. Discussed with PIC and proper date marking was added. Ensure that TCS foods stored in house longer than 24 hours after opening are date marked and discarded if not used within 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: A sanitizer bucket was being stored directly next to the meatballs on the steam table. Discussed with PIC and the sani bucket was moved to a different location. Ensure that chemicals are never stored in a manner that can contaminate food items.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The bottom shelf of the prep cooler near the drive thru window was heavily accumulated with food debris and spilled liquids. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent buildup.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Two soda machines that appear to be in disrepair are being stored in the lobby next to the service station. The pieces of equipment are leaking syrups onto the floor, which can also attract unwanted pest and insects. Remove soda machines if they are no longer serving a purpose to the facility.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.
